slides.lead: 18 months and not saying much yet?
slides.sub: What is typical, what is a wide range, and what is worth a conversation.

slides.head: When first words tend to arrive
slides.body: First words often come around the first birthday, with wide variation. By 18 months most children try to say three or more words beyond "mama" and "dada". Understanding runs well ahead of speech the whole time.

slides.head: What matters more than the word count
slides.body:
At this age the signs of communication are mostly not words. Pointing to show you something. Following a simple instruction without a gesture. Looking where you look. Taking turns with sounds.

A child doing those things with few words is usually on a wide, normal path.

slides.head: Worth a conversation with your paediatrician
items: Not pointing or gesturing to share something with you
Not responding to their name most of the time
Very little eye contact or back-and-forth
Words they used to say that have gone
A lag across several areas, not one
slides.note: Not a diagnosis. A reason to ask, early.

slides.head: This week
items: Narrate what she is looking at, not what you want her to look at.
Treat every sound as a turn. Answer it, then wait.
Read the same book again. Pause before the word she knows is coming.
slides.note: Interaction builds language; exposure alone does not.
